solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Applicant for role of jester around British court?

indicators.note: the jester's word is wrapped around the other pieces, splitting after its second letter

parts.note: a joker is a jester, a clown who makes people laugh
the Holy See is the papal court, and a bishop's see is his seat and court

explanation.surface: A clown hoping to land a part at the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' is not woo here: the Holy See is the papal court, and a see is a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hunting for a job is an applicant for a post or role.

clue.text: Company brought in to inoculate sheep

indicators.note: brought in says the company goes inside the injection word

parts.note: to jab is to give an injection, inoculate

explanation.surface: A firm hired to vaccinate a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacob is a piebald breed of sheep with multiple horns.

clue.text: Squandered about a million once before your boss denied fellow culpability

indicators.note: the squandered word goes about the next two pieces

parts.note: blew, as in blew the money, means squandered
or is an archaic word for before, as in 'or ever'
thine is the old form of your or yours

indicators.note: denied means the boss is deprived of the fellow's letters

parts.note: taken as written
bo is American slang for a fellow or pal

explanation.surface: A spendthrift lost a fortune and the boss refused to blame an underling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks archaic usage: OR for before and THINE for your. BO is American slang for a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Blameworthiness is the state of deserving blame, which is culpability.

clue.text: A measure of change?

parts.note: a measure is a dance, and in this dance partners are changed when one cuts in politely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' looks like a gauge of how much has changed, but it is an old word for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse-me is a dance where a person may interrupt and take over another's partner.

clue.text: Oil treatment for sore knee

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are worked on and handled into a new form

explanation.surface: Rubbing oil into a painful knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin, a fuel oil distilled from petroleum.

clue.text: District with central area and private central zone

indicators.note: central picks out the middle letters of area

parts.note: a GI is a US private soldier
the central pair of letters of zone, taken the same way as the middle of area

explanation.surface: An urban district with a public centre and a private central quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' works twice: once on area and again on zone, each time keeping the middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or territory, which a district also is.

clue.text: Set subject to photograph

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photograph

explanation.surface: An instruction to make some subject the focus of a photo shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or subject given for discussion or an essay, a set subject.

clue.text: Time to fix support for pot over fire

parts.note: to rivet is to fasten or fix

explanation.surface: Time to mend the stand that holds a cooking pot over a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged stand for setting a pot or kettle above the flames.

clue.text: Take retrograde step and create remit, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: return to an earlier, outdated state of affairs
second meaning, read literally: write a timer, one kind of clock, back to front and you create remit

explanation.walkthrough: Remit is timer spelt backwards, and a timer is a sort of clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to undo progress and return to old ways, a backward move.

clue.text: Conservative offer is one in opposition

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer

explanation.surface: A Tory proposal is put forward by a member of the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a rival or competitor, someone pitted against others.

clue.text: Opportunist not unknown in court

indicators.note: not tells us to go without the unknown, dropping it from the court's name

parts.note: Chancery is a division of the English High Court
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: A schemer who was absent from the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is British slang for someone who takes risks to exploit any opportunity.

clue.text: Flash singlet, belted

indicators.note: belted suggests the letters were hit about, knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A showy vest pulled in with a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' reads as an adjective for the singlet but is the verb meaning to sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine or sparkle, so a verb sense of flash.

clue.text: Bishop has not so much to call holy

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A bishop with fewer duties than usual for consecrating things.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless is to consecrate, to pronounce something sacred or holy.

clue.text: Pottery shop introducing contemporary note

indicators.note: the shop takes in the other pieces, introducing them into its middle

parts.note: a store is a shop
new means modern, contemporary
A is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: A ceramics shop bringing in a modern musical touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense, hard type of fired clay ware, a kind of pottery.

clue.text: Like florist's goods — doing well, bringing in pounds

indicators.note: the booming word brings the pounds sign inside itself

parts.note: a booming business is thriving, doing well
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A flower shop's trade thriving and taking in money.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers sold by a florist are in bloom, so blooming describes them.

clue.text: Book a very good act

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1924 adventure novel by P. C. Wren about the French Foreign Legion
second meaning: French for a fine or gracious gesture

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests praising a stage performance; the phrase is both a novel's title and a borrowed French expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau geste is French for a noble gesture and the title of a famous Foreign Legion novel.

clue.text: Small child's slide

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a kid is a child; the 's is read as 'has' linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A little one's playground slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is an uncontrolled sliding movement, as of a car on ice.

clue.text: Harshness of truth coming after half of lies raised

indicators.note: coming after puts truth's word behind the reversed half
raised, in a down clue, means the kept half is turned upwards, read backwards
half of means only the back two letters of lies are kept

parts.note: verity means truth

explanation.surface: How harsh the truth seems when it follows a pack of lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the back half of LIES, and in a down clue 'raised' reads that pair upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity is sternness or strictness, the quality of being harsh.

clue.text: Shrub needing fantastic drainage

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wild, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A bush that requires superb soil drainage.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Man's raised voice in loyal toast

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting inside the words loyal toast

explanation.surface: A man raising his voice during the loyal toast to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The loyal toast is a toast to the sovereign at British formal dinners.
explanation.definitionFit: A male alto, or countertenor, sings in a register raised above the normal male range.

clue.text: Calling son a donkey perhaps upset mother and pa

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad were upset when their boy was called a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a donkey is figurative speech, a comparison by figure rather than literal fact.

clue.text: Woolly breed of cattle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a woolly is British for a knitted sweater
second meaning: a dairy cow from the Channel Island

explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly' reads as an adjective describing the cattle, but it is a noun for a knitted garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted pullover and also a Channel Island dairy breed.

clue.text: Pub getting in cut fish

indicators.note: the pub's word gets in between the letters of the cutting word

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub receiving a delivery of trimmed fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a small freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Pointer's good in Scotland and English border

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good
a line can be a border or boundary

explanation.surface: A pointer dog that is well behaved in Scotland and along the English border.
explanation.definitionFit: A guideline is a piece of advice or a rule of thumb that points the way.

clue.text: 100 entering to praise returning noble

indicators.note: the hundred goes into the reversed word
returning means the word for praise is read backwards

parts.note: to laud is to praise
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A century of people come in to acclaim a nobleman on his return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LAUD to DUAL, and 'entering' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means of a duke, the highest rank of the nobility.

clue.text: Failure further down when changing points

indicators.note: points are compass points, so one compass letter is swapped for another, west for south

parts.note: lower means further down

explanation.surface: A team sinking lower in the table after a change in its points tally.
explanation.walkthrough: W (west) and S (south) are both compass points; swap one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who habitually fails, a failure.

clue.text: Walks over relative

parts.note: steps, as a verb, means walks or paces
on can mean over, as in a lid sitting on a box

explanation.surface: Someone trampling a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, 'steps on' means walks over; split, it gives the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a spouse's son from an earlier relationship, a relation by marriage.

clue.text: Shiny granite close-up is regularly — this?

definitions.text: Shiny granite close-up is regularly — this?

indicators.note: regularly means picking letters at an even interval, here every third letter starting from the third

explanation.surface: Looking closely at polished granite and asking what kind of rock it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every third letter of 'Shiny granite close-up is', starting at the I. The whole clue also defines: granite is the textbook example of this rock type.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is formed from cooled magma, which makes it a volcanic-origin or fire-formed rock.

clue.text: Attempt broadcast of a certain appeal?

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the letters are spoken

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal, coyly called a certain appeal

explanation.surface: A trial transmission of some kind of plea.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters S and A, spoken one after the other, make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to try it, and an essay is an attempt.

clue.text: Sign with pen after practice

indicators.note: after places the pen's word behind the practice's word

parts.note: a way is a habit or custom, a practice
a marker is a felt-tip pen

explanation.surface: Signing your name with a pen once you have practised.
explanation.definitionFit: A waymarker is a post or symbol marking a footpath route for walkers.
